prose_updates.tldr: Two conditionally independent assignment waves on one no-carryover schedule identify the Palm population covariance through observable cross-wave IPW products. A joint assignment--innovation cylinder version, common to every assignment outside one null set, explicitly induces every finite exposure, outcome, propensity, and score coordinate on the buffered interior. Explicit radius-one Rademacher witnesses use the Borel cylinders \(\Psi^{\Delta}(u,x)=(x_0,(u_0-u_{-1})x_0)\) and \(\Psi^+(u,x)=(x_0,u_0x_0)\) with the single null set empty; they show that zero long-run variance can coexist with heterogeneous local scores and that the positive-variance alternative is nonempty. These primitives give order-\(n^{-1}\) centering bias and root-\(n\) finite-sample concentration, size and power, and an exactly unbiased lag-separated statistic. A verified four-cell local schedule has common support at the level of the complete buffered graph--assignment--exposure--outcome record and proves a matching full-observation minimax lower bound. Thus, for distinct focal labels, both the full-observation and score-vector separation radii are \(\Theta(n^{-1/2})\) for fixed \(r,B,\varepsilon,\alpha,\beta\), \(p=1/2\), and \(\alpha+\beta<1\).

project_justification.fill: The project proves the cross-wave identity, order-\(n^{-1}\) centering control, root-\(n\) concentration, finite-sample size and power, and an exactly unbiased lag-separated statistic under the corrected common local versions. The explicit radius-one cylinders \(\Psi^{\Delta}(u,x)=(x_0,(u_0-u_{-1})x_0)\) and \(\Psi^+(u,x)=(x_0,u_0x_0)\), both valid with the empty exceptional set, certify a heterogeneous zero-variance boundary point and a positive-variance point in the same local class. For distinct focal exposure labels, the project also constructs a causal-realizable four-cell submodel with \(\operatorname{KL}\le2N_nt^2\) for the complete declared record and linearly changing \(\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}\), yielding matching \(\Theta(n^{-1/2})\) minimax rates for the full observation and its score-vector subexperiment.

prose_updates.interpretation: The null \(\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}=0\) is a covariance-cancellation boundary, not a claim that conditional exposure effects are homogeneous. The explicit law \(P^{\Delta}\) has \(h_i=U_i-U_{i-1}\), variance \(2\) at each site, lag-one covariances \(-1\), and long-run sum zero; \(P^+\) has \(h_i=U_i\) and long-run variance one. Both laws satisfy the corrected left-shift orientation and the joint radius-one cylinder condition with one empty exceptional set. On the line, the joint cylinder condition makes the conditional score a finite block factor, so Janson's result represents the null score as a finite-block coboundary. Rejection certifies positive Palm population variation; failure to reject only places that variation within the stated finite-sample threshold.

statement_notes.justification: The paired laws explicitly satisfy the joint assignment--innovation cylinder premise with the single null set empty, verifying that the null contains heterogeneous conditional scores and that the positive-variance alternative is nonempty under one common envelope.
statement_notes.gap: LiWager2022 discusses assignment-dominated limits in a dense graphon setting; these exact radius-one line examples instead exhibit covariance cancellation and positive Palm variation inside the diagnostic's corrected common-cylinder class.
statement_notes.consumer: The two fully specified local laws provide finite-range simulation benchmarks for null rejection frequencies and power calculations, with their Palm population variances equal to zero and one exactly.
